ripplet_v1: Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: game-ready pixel sprite sheet for Godot, NOT a concept poster. Reference image: the approved Wildbond starter concept board; use ONLY the CENTER creature RIPPLET, preserving its exact identity. Ripplet is a small expressive turquoise biped river lizard, cream belly, dark blue backward swept head fin, large yellow eyes, blue-and-white wave-shaped neck frill, yellow cheek marks, long curled blue tail. Preserve the wave frill and proportions, simplify painterly details into clean readable pixel clusters. Match Nintendo DS-era monster sprite craft: restrained palette, dark navy single-pixel outlines, 3-tone shading, upper-left light, crisp stair-stepped edges, NO smooth illustration, NO antialiasing, NO blur. Transparent background with real alpha. No text, labels, grid lines, floor, shadows, bubbles or detached effects. Sheet EXACT 1024 wide by 1536 tall, 4 columns and 6 rows of 256x256 cells. Each sprite FULLY INSIDE its cell with at least 20px clear margin, especially tail/frill; no body parts crossing cells. Render underlying pixels at consistent 4x nearest-neighbor magnification. TOP ROW: four large battle sprites, approximately 50-54 logical pixels high (200-216 image pixels): columns1/2 the same front three-quarter view facing lower-left, neutral eyes open then a subtle closed-eye blink; columns3/4 the same rear three-quarter view facing upper-right, neutral then a subtle breathing pose. ROWS2-6: small overworld sprites approximately 26 logical pixels high (104 image pixels), centered horizontally, feet at the same baseline y=208 within each cell; a genuinely elevated RPG camera showing tops of head and shoulders, not side-view concept art. Row2 facing DOWN toward camera, Row3 DOWN-RIGHT, Row4 RIGHT profile, Row5 UP-RIGHT rear diagonal, Row6 UP true rear with no face visible. Each overworld row is a four-frame walk cycle: left foot forward, neutral passing, right foot forward, neutral passing, clear alternating footfall and small tail counter-sway; all four frames keep identical scale, anatomy, frill and palette. Front and rear views must be genuinely different; maintain recognizable head-fin/frill silhouettes in back views. Ensure isolated complete silhouettes with no clipping. Reproduce the approved creature, not a new redesign.
ripplet_v2: Use case: style-transfer. Edit this RIPPLET sprite sheet ONLY to make its pixel density appropriate for actual DS-era game sprites. Preserve ALL 24 complete characters, their exact order, every view, the approved anatomy, turquoise/cream/dark-blue palette, wave frill, head fin, yellow eyes and curled tail. Preserve transparent alpha background, remove any near-transparent matte haze. Do not introduce text, grid lines, shadows, scene or effects. Biggest correction: draw in visibly COARSE PIXEL ART. Each conceptual pixel must be a solid 4x4 square in this 1024x1536 output, with the entire image aligned to the same 4-pixel grid; NO 1px/2px hairlines, NO dithering, NO watercolor or fine fur/wave texture, NO antialiasing. Use no more than 20 solid colors plus transparent, compact outlined pixel clusters and two/three clean shades per hue. Battle characters in row1 should read as roughly 60x72 native pixel sprites magnified4x. The 20 walking characters in rows2-6 should read as roughly 36x48 native pixels magnified4x, with consistent scale within every row. Keep all toes and tails inside separated transparent margins. The front battle view can face right; the engine will mirror it. Rear battle view is genuinely from behind. Walking rows must remain down, down-right, right, up-right, up, four alternating-leg walking poses each. Keep the same overall layout/row spacing. This must look like a hand-crafted playable sprite sheet viewed at integer zoom, not an illustration with a pixelated filter.
